report_name: Ochsner Health Confirms Data Breach Involving Microsoft System

attack_patterns.name: Email Forwarding Rule
attack_patterns.description: The report recommends hunting for the creation of new inbox rules that forward email externally, a common tactic for maintaining access and exfiltrating data from compromised Microsoft 365 accounts.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The report recommends hunting for suspicious sign-ins to Microsoft Azure AD accounts, such as those exhibiting impossible travel, originating from unfamiliar locations, or coming from anonymous IP addresses (VPN/Tor).

attack_patterns.name: Create Account: Cloud Account
attack_patterns.description: The report recommends alerting on the creation of new accounts with administrative rights in the Microsoft cloud environment as a key detection strategy.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Information Repositories
attack_patterns.description: The report recommends monitoring for unusual file access patterns in SharePoint/OneDrive and the initiation of eDiscovery searches, which could indicate attacker data collection activities.

identities.name: Ochsner Health
identities.description: A major non-profit healthcare provider based in Louisiana that was the victim of a data breach originating from a compromise within its Microsoft-based systems.

indicators.name: M365 Inbox Forwarding Rule Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: M365 Inbox Forwarding Rule Creation
id: 2b8a1b9e-7c3d-4f8a-9b1e-8d6a4f2c1b9e
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a new inbox rule that forwards email to an external address. This is a common technique for data exfiltration and persistence.
references:
  - https://hsecurities.in/blog/ochsner-health-data-breach-microsoft-confirmation
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-21
tags:
  - attack.t1114.003
level: high
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.exchange
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'New-InboxRule'
    Parameters.ForwardTo|exists: true
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of a new inbox rule in Microsoft 365 that forwards emails, a technique mentioned as a hunting hint in the report.

indicators.name: Anomalous M365 Sign-in from Anonymous IP
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous M365 Sign-in from Anonymous IP
id: 5d9c3a1b-8e4f-4a2d-8b1a-9c3d8a1b9e4f
status: experimental
description: Detects successful Azure AD sign-ins from an anonymous IP address (e.g., Tor, anonymous VPN), which is a recommended hunting hint for cloud account compromise.
references:
  - https://hsecurities.in/blog/ochsner-health-data-breach-microsoft-confirmation
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-21
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    Status.errorCode: 0
    RiskDetail: 'anonymousIpAddress'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects successful sign-ins to Azure AD from anonymous IP addresses, a hunting hint provided in the article for detecting compromised cloud accounts.

indicators.name: M365 eDiscovery Search Started
indicators.pattern:
title: M365 eDiscovery Search Started
id: 9e1b8d6a-4f2c-4b9e-8a1b-9e7c3d4f8a9b
status: experimental
description: Detects the start of an eDiscovery search in Microsoft 365. While a legitimate admin tool, its unexpected use can indicate an attacker collecting data from SharePoint or OneDrive.
references:
  - https://hsecurities.in/blog/ochsner-health-data-breach-microsoft-confirmation
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-21
tags:
  - attack.t1213
level: medium
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.core
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'Start-eDiscoverySearch'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the initiation of an eDiscovery search, a recommended monitoring point in the article for identifying data collection from SharePoint/OneDrive.
